    AI Overview
    what
    /(h)wət/
    "What" is a versatile English interrogative word used to inquire about the identity, nature, or value of an object, action, or idea. It acts as a pronoun, determiner, or adverb, often highlighting that options are unlimited, unlike "which". It also expresses surprise ("What, no lunch?") or acts as a filler ("You know what?"). 
    Usage Examples & Contexts 
    • Asking for Information: "What time is it?" or "What do you want?".
    • Determiner (Specific Object): "What books do you read?".
    • Exclamation (Emphasis): "What a lovely day!".
    • Referring to Unknown Things: "I know what happened".
    • Idioms: "What for" (why), "What's up" (what is happening), "Know what’s what" (understand details). 
    Synonyms & Related Terms 
    • Interrogative: Which, whatever.
    • Noun usage (the what): Entity, thing, substance.
    • Exclamatory: How (e.g., "how remarkable"). 
    What vs. Which 
    • Use what for open-ended questions with many possibilities (e.g., "What is your favorite food?").
    • Use which when there is a restricted or limited set of options (e.g., "Which drink do you want, tea or coffee?").
